trimmingSuggestions.description: The repetitive use of title cards for each step (especially Steps 3-9) could be minimized. Consider combining some steps into a single screen or using subtle on-screen graphics instead of full-screen title cards to maintain visual interest.
The host could visually demonstrate some steps (like setting the camera to landscape mode) while explaining them to add dynamism and show rather than just tell.
Briefly showing examples of good and bad framing or lighting at the end could strengthen the advice and leave a lasting impact.

text_to_speech: Can't make it to the auditions? We'll help you create a tape. Effortlessly! Right at your home! Everyone gets nervous... But confidence is the key to everything and the most important point. Choose a solid, light coloured background or wall Make sure your lighting is really good. When you are using a natural light the light should fall on your face. Set the camera on landscape mode. Get the camera as close to you as possible for better audio. Not so close also that your face looks distorted Make sure your frame is from head to mid waist or chest. Depending on how much your camera can fit. When stating your contact details... include only asked details Like name, age, mobile number, email ID and your side profiles. While finally auditioning, never look directly into the camera. Look somewhere off camera like here or here. (behind camera) Lastly, avoid as much movement as possible for less distraction. and keep it as simple as possible. We hope this video was useful to you. You can now send in your audition videos. On the link given in the comment box.

How to shoot an audition with your smartphone camera?
Use a tripod, if you don't have one place your smartphone or camera on a desk, chair, ledge or shelf.

Choose a light coloured wall as the background. If there are any switches, etc stand in front of the switch box to cover it.

Make sure that you light your face well. If you're shooting with natural light face the light so that the light brightens up your face. 

If you know how, lock your exposure and focus settings or your smartphone or camera app.

Use landscape orientation. Don't shoot on portrait mode.

Set the camera close to you so that you get less noise and better audio.

Frame a mid shot, keep a little space above your head down to your waist or chest.

Start your audition stating your name, age, contact details and phone number. Make sure to turn sideways to show your profile shot or even pan down to show your entire body.

Don't look directly into the camera unless asked to. Look off camera or behind the camera.

Keep your actions and movements to the minimum, try and be expressive with your eyes and face instead. Don't wave your hands and block your face.
